title: Putting It All Together: A Whole Story

sections.title: Every piece, in one story
sections.content: You now have everything you need for a short story: a place and time to open it, aztán/utána/később to move it along, amikor to set a scene, egyszer csak or hirtelen for the surprise, azt mondta hogy to bring in someone else's words, and az elején/a végén to frame the whole thing. Here's what a complete short story looks like when several of them work together.

sections.title: A complete short story
rows: At the beginning we traveled to Vienna, Károly and I.
Amikor sétáltunk a városban, egyszer csak elkezdett esni.
When we were walking in the city, all of a sudden it started to rain.
A végén boldogan hazamentünk, és mindent elmeséltem Petrának.
In the end we went home happily, and I told Petra everything.

items.spanish: Az elején Bécsbe utaztunk, aztán sétáltunk a városban, és a végén boldogan hazamentünk.
items.english: At the beginning we traveled to Vienna, then we walked around the city, and in the end we went home happily.

items.spanish: Károly azt mondta, hogy ez volt egy nagyon vicces történet.
items.english: Károly said that this was a very funny story.

items.spanish: Amikor hazamentünk, elmeséltem Petrának az egész történetet.
items.english: When we went home, I told Petra the whole story.

sections.content: A good short story rarely needs every tool at once — pick two or three (a scene-setting amikor, one surprise, one closing az elején/a végén frame) and let them carry the story, the same restraint Unit 25's tip suggested for előbb/aztán/végül.
